subject: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme TCO & next steps

Hi Alex —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and the cost/TCO levers we discussed so your team has a single reference. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points you mentioned
- High per-call cost for large batch request volumes (inference on 1.5B token/month workload).
- Unpredictable latency spikes and token overage risk during peak trading windows.
- Limited observability into token/route-level costs for engineering teams and finance.

Goals
- Reduce inference unit cost by 30–40% while keeping <200ms p95 latency for critical routes.
- Predictable monthly spend for budgeting and procurement.
- Integration with existing SSO/KMS and audit log requirements.

Cost/TCO framing (rough numbers from call)
- Baseline: current vendor ~ $1.25 per 1k tokens delivered (avg model mix).
- Redwood baseline projection (no batching/optimization): ~$0.70 per 1k tokens.
- With recommended levers (batching + prefix/KV caching + quantized model variant): ~$0.38–0.45 per 1k tokens (depends on mix of short/long sequences).
- Example ROI: for 1.5B tokens/month, that’s ~$570k/month -> with optimizations ~$285k–$420k/month (30–50% savings).

Recommended levers we discussed
1) Batch-friendly routing: group short, low-latency requests into micro-batches during peak windows (saves ~15–25% on token cost for that traffic).
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated context across sessions (especially for system prompts and common user histories) — we estimated 10–20% effective token reduction for your usage patterns.
3) Quantized model variant for non-critical long-form generation (4-bit quant): reduces GPU cost per token with minimal quality impact on those routes.
4) Route-based SLAs: keep critical routes pinned to the low-latency pool and route cheaper requests to capacity-optimized backfills.

Next steps
- I attached a first-pass TCO model with assumptions (redwood-tco-analysis.xlsx). Please share any billing/export we should align to (token mix, p95 targets).
- Rafael (cc) will prepare a short SRE/SE session to show batching/caching config and run live estimates.
- If procurement wants numbers, looping in Lisa/Procurement would make sense to finalize SOW and budget cadence.

Available slots: Wed 6/16 10–12 PT or Thu 6/17 14–16 PT for a 30-min follow-up.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side:
- Can you provide the per-1k token number for the quantized variant and the non-quantized baseline separately? We need line items for procurement.
- For batching, what is the expected latency delta for critical routes if we micro-batch? We can tolerate up to +25ms p95 on some non-core flows but need <200ms for our trading alerts.
- Our CFO (Lisa) asked for a 12-month spend projection including forecasted traffic growth + buffer for burst windows.

Budget constraints: we have a hard ceiling for Q3 of $3.2M for LLM infra (all vendors). Any ROI framing you can provide versus current annualized run rate would help.

Open to the Wed slot — please send the invite. Also procurement is copied for SOW discussions.

—Alex

Alex — thanks, answers inline below and attached an updated model (redwood-tco-analysis-v2.xlsx) with a 12-month projection and breakouts by lever.

Per-1k token numbers (estimates, final depends on exact token mix and sequence lengths)
- Current vendor (your baseline reported): $1.25 / 1k tokens
- Redwood baseline (hosted, default model mix, no batching/quant): $0.70 / 1k tokens
- Redwood with quantized variant (4-bit) for long-form: $0.45 / 1k tokens
- Redwood with batching + KV caching + quantized routing applied to appropriate routes: $0.38 / 1k tokens

Latency impact for batching
- Micro-batching short requests (batch windows 5–10ms): measured p95 delta ~+10–20ms for short routes — within your +25ms tolerance for non-core flows.
- Critical trading alert route: we recommend pinning to a low-latency pool (no micro-batching) — that keeps p95 <200ms. All other routes can be batched.

12-month spend projection (high level, see attached sheet)
- Year 1 baseline (current vendor): ~$3.6M annualized for your current 1.5B tokens/month profile.
- Redwood predicted Year 1 w/optimizations: ~$1.7M–$2.9M depending on adoption of levers (conservative -> $2.9M, recommended mix -> ~$2.0M).
- That maps to a potential 20–53% annual savings vs current run rate; detailed scenarios in the attached model.

Attachments in this email: redwood-tco-analysis-v2.xlsx, draft-SOW.pdf

Proposed next steps
1) Rafael to run a short SE session showing live batching/KV cache demo and run a traffic-profile-based estimate.
2) We’ll share a redlined SOW draft and pricing tiers for procurement (attached).
3) If these numbers look good, we can do a 30-day pilot with capacity commit for a predictable unit cost and monitoring hooks.

I tentatively scheduled Wed 6/16 10:30 PT — invite to follow. Rafael/Nikhil, please confirm availability.
